findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff changes the signatures of wire-provided constructors — ProvideAnonDBStore gains a deviceLimit parameter and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService swaps anonStore anonstore.AnonStore for sqlStore db.DB — but the committed generated injection file pkg/server/wire_gen.go, which calls both functions, is not regenerated in this diff. go build ./... fails to compile: wire_gen.go still calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) with one argument and passes an anonstore.AnonStore into the parameter that is now db.DB, so every CI run and local build of this PR breaks until wire is regenerated.

[BUG] TagDevice writes the device into the local cache before the limit-enforcing write executes (the cache Set sits ahead of the tagDeviceUI call and nothing between the new `return err` and `return nil` touches the cache), so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached is a cache hit on its next request, TagDevice returns nil, and Authenticate grants the anonymous identity. device_limit never caps the actual device population: each new device is rejected exactly once per ~29-minute cache window and admitted on every retry, so operators who configure device_limit get effectively unlimited anonymous devices plus periodic unexplained 401s instead of the configured cap.

[ADVISORY] The fire-and-forget tagging goroutine (detached context.Background with a 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) is replaced with a synchronous TagDevice call inside Authenticate, so every anonymous request with a cold local-cache entry now blocks inline on the CountDevices + upsert database roundtrips that previously ran in the background. Database latency or saturation now directly stalls anonymous authentication on Grafana's hottest request path, and a hung tagging write blocks the user's request for as long as the request context lives instead of being capped by the old 2-minute background timeout.

[ADVISORY] The ErrDeviceLimitReached branch returns nil, err without any log statement (a.log.Warn is only reached for other errors), so the new request-rejecting path emits no log line from the component that produces the rejection. Operators who enable device_limit see anonymous users start receiving 401s with nothing in the anonimpl logs explaining why, making the feature's primary user-visible behavior undiagnosable in production.

[ADVISORY] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-upsert sequence, so concurrent first-seen devices all observe count < deviceLimit and each take the unconditional INSERT path. Under concurrent first requests the anon_device table can exceed device_limit by the number of racing requests; the conditional UPDATE in updateDevice only guards the already-saturated case, so the configured limit is not a hard bound.

[ADVISORY] The only new test exercises the store in isolation; no test in the diff covers the behavior this PR actually ships — TagDevice propagating ErrDeviceLimitReached, the local-cache interaction with the limit check, or client.go failing the authentication. A regression in the propagation or cache path — exactly where the cache can admit limit-rejected devices — passes CI silently and only surfaces as unexplained 401s or a silently disabled limit in production.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day window is now defined twice as anonymousDeviceExpiration — once in anonimpl/api/api.go (renamed from thirtyDays) and once in anonimpl/anonstore/database.go — with no shared source of truth. A future change to one window (the device API's listing window vs the limiter's enforcement window) silently diverges the two, and nothing flags the drift between what the API reports and what the limiter enforces.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceLimit is added to the GrafanaConfig interface (grafana-data), GrafanaBootConfig, and the frontend-settings DTO, but nothing in the diff or the frontend reads it — enforcement is entirely server-side. Three pieces of public surface across the Go/TS boundary ship with zero consumers and must be kept type-compatible indefinitely, with no user-visible benefit until some future UI actually consumes the value.

[BUG] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService's signature is changed (anonStore parameter replaced by sqlStore db.DB) and ProvideAnonDBStore gains a non-injectable int64 parameter, but the diff contains no update to any wire provider set or to the generated wire_gen.go that calls these constructors. The tree as diffed does not compile / fails the wire check: the checked-in generated wiring still calls ProvideAnonymousDeviceService with the old argument list, and wire cannot satisfy the new int64 parameter of ProvideAnonDBStore if it remains in a provider set, so the PR is missing a required build artifact.

[BUG] The device-limit enforcement in CreateOrUpdateDevice is a non-atomic count-then-insert: concurrent requests for distinct new devices both read count < deviceLimit and both proceed to INSERT. When the count equals deviceLimit-1 and two new devices tag concurrently — exactly the burst scenario the limit exists to control — both rows are inserted and the stored device count exceeds the configured cap; the limit is not actually enforced under concurrency (no transaction, lock, or unique guard backs the check).

[ADVISORY] The new auth.anonymous 'device_limit' key is parsed in readAuthSettings but no corresponding entry is added to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini anywhere in the diff. Operators cannot discover the setting or learn that 0 means unlimited from the canonical config files, and the in-repo config documentation silently diverges from the keys Grafana actually parses — the setting is effectively undocumented at merge.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts that a NEW device id is rejected once the cap is reached; no test in the diff exercises an existing device successfully updating via updateDevice while the limit is reached, nor an existing device with a stale (>30d) updated_at being rejected. The feature's core promise — existing active devices keep working at the cap — is unverified; a regression in updateDevice's SQL (wrong column, wrong window bounds) would lock out every anonymous device once the limit is hit and no test in this diff would fail.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (background context, 2-minute timeout, panic recovery) onto the synchronous authentication path, with no negative caching for rejected devices. Every anonymous authentication on a local-cache miss now blocks on a synchronous COUNT(*) plus write, so anonstore latency directly delays login; a device rejected by the limit is never cached, so each subsequent request from it repeats count+update on the auth critical path; and the removed recover() means a panic inside TagDevice now fails the request instead of being logged.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers the new error branch in Authenticate — neither that ErrDeviceLimitReached aborts anonymous authentication nor that non-limit tagging errors still yield a working anonymous identity. A regression that swallows ErrDeviceLimitReached (limit silently unenforced) or that propagates ordinary DB errors (anonymous access breaks whenever anonstore is degraded) ships undetected; the diff's test files (database_test.go, impl_test.go) touch neither branch of this the most user-visible behavior in the PR.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration is now defined twice with the same value — unexported in anonstore/database.go and again in api/api.go (renamed from thirtyDays) — as two independent constants with no shared source of truth. Changing the device retention in one package silently diverges the limit-counting window from the admin listing window, so devices shown to admins in the API would no longer match the devices counted against the cap; exporting the store constant deletes the duplicate and the drift hazard.

[ADVISORY] When the cap is hit the limit-reached path returns before the Warn log (only a Debug line in TagDevice fires), and the newly exposed boot-config field anonymousDeviceLimit has no consumer anywhere in the diff. Once an instance reaches its cap, new anonymous users get Grafana's generic unauthenticated failure while the server emits no log at default level recording why, and no frontend or admin surface distinguishes 'device limit reached' from a broken instance — operators troubleshoot a silent self-inflicted lockout.

[ADVISORY] The cap is a single global count over all anonymous devices while device identity is (client_ip, user_agent)-based per the Device schema, and user_agent is client-controlled. One actor minting deviceLimit distinct device IDs (e.g., by varying User-Agent from one address) saturates the global count and denies anonymous access to every new visitor until entries age out of the 30-day window; the diff scopes the limit neither per-IP nor per-org, and documents or alerts on this lockout nowhere.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice infers 'device unknown → limit reached' from rowsAffected == 0, but on MySQL an UPDATE that matches a row yet changes no values also reports 0 affected rows. An existing active device re-tagged within the same stored-timestamp second (e.g., a duplicate tag landing on a second instance with a cold local cache while the cap is reached) produces an identical-value UPDATE, gets rowsAffected 0, and is wrongly rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, blocking a legitimate device the limit is meant to keep working.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-insert check (separate sessions, no transaction, lock, or conditional insert), so concurrent first-time tags all observe count < limit and all insert. With device_limit=N, a burst of new anonymous devices (exactly the traffic the limit targets) leaves N+k active rows in anon_device; the configured cap is not the cap that holds, and the over-limit state persists until the 30-day cleanup runs. The core invariant of the feature is only enforced in the single-threaded happy path.

[ADVISORY] The new device_limit option is read from the auth.anonymous ini section but this diff does not add it to conf/defaults.ini or the configuration docs, so the setting ships without its documented configuration surface. Operators upgrading Grafana cannot discover device_limit in defaults.ini or the generated configuration reference — the 'configurable' half of 'add configurable device limit' is invisible, and the feature is effectively unusable except by reading the source.

[ADVISORY] The diff plumbs anonymousDeviceLimit into the frontend boot config (grafana-data type, grafana-runtime default, FrontendSettingsDTO, getFrontendSettings) without adding any consumer, so an unread value is shipped in every frontend settings payload. Dead API surface across three packages plus an always-present field in every /api/frontend/settings response; it also discloses the configured anonymous device capacity to unauthenticated visitors, who can use it to size device rotation against the cap, and it becomes a second place to keep in sync (or rip out) when the real frontend work lands.

[ADVISORY] Authenticate now runs TagDevice synchronously on the request path (the fire-and-forget goroutine is removed), and devices rejected by the limit are never successfully tagged and so never populate the 29-minute local cache, making every over-limit request execute a synchronous COUNT over anon_device plus a zero-row UPDATE before being rejected. Anonymous request latency now includes blocking DB round-trips for every uncached device, and the feature adds per-request database load precisely for the over-limit/rotating-device traffic it is meant to shed — a self-inflicted amplification under the exact abuse scenario the limit exists for.

[ADVISORY] The only limit>0 test exercises the rejection path (rowsAffected == 0); no test in the diff exercises updateDevice's success path — an existing, in-window device re-tagging while the limit is reached — which is the steady-state path for every returning device on a limit-enabled instance. A regression in updateDevice's WHERE window (the UTC conversions and 30-day arithmetic) would reject every anonymous device once the instance is at capacity — a full anonymous-access outage — and no test in this diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] Converting the tagging goroutine to a synchronous call deletes the recover() guard that previously contained panics from device tagging, so a panic in the tagging path now propagates into the auth middleware and fails the request. A panic while parsing/hash-ing untrusted request headers (the reason the recover existed) turns every affected anonymous request into a 500, where previously the panic was logged as a warning and the request was served anonymously.

[ADVISORY] The new enforcement branches — returning the limit error from Authenticate to block anonymous auth, log-and-continue for other tagging errors, and impl.go's new unconditional `return err` from TagDevice — have no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression that drops the errors.Is check, wraps the error in a way errors.Is misses, or re-swallows it in TagDevice silently disables the entire enforcement point while every store-level test still passes.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device expiration is now defined twice as identically-named package-local constants — anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore (database.go) and anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonimpl/api (api.go, renamed from thirtyDays) — with no shared source of truth. Changing one constant silently desyncs the admin ListDevices window from the limit's count/update window, so operators using the debugging API to investigate a reached limit see a device set that no longer matches what enforcement counts.

[ADVISORY] The TS contract declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined with an undefined default, but the Go DTO serializes the field unconditionally (no omitempty on AnonymousDeviceLimit int64), so the boot payload always carries a number (0 when unset) and undefined is unreachable. The first frontend consumer branching on `config.anonymousDeviceLimit === undefined` to detect 'no limit configured' never takes that branch, because the backend always sends 0; the declared type documents a shape the payload never produces.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-insert, so concurrent first-visit requests all read count < limit and all insert. With device_limit=N, a burst of N+M simultaneous new devices inserts N+M rows — the cap is exceeded under exactly the concurrent load it exists to control, and a client fanning out parallel device IDs defeats it deliberately; no unique constraint, conditional insert, or row lock serializes the check.

[BUG] ErrDeviceLimitReached is a bare fmt.Errorf with no typed HTTP mapping, so a limit denial fails anonymous authentication with an error the authn middleware can only render as a generic 500 'Internal server error' rather than a deliberate 4xx. Once the limit is hit, every first-visit anonymous request returns a 500, generating server-error alerts and an unexplained error page for an operator-configured capacity condition instead of a meaningful 403/429 response.

[BUG] TagDevice moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine bounded by a 2-minute context.WithTimeout to a synchronous call on the request context with no deadline, putting anon_device store latency directly on the anonymous authentication path. A slow or hung anon_device database (pool exhaustion, network black hole) now stalls every anonymous request for the driver's full TCP timeout, where previously the request completed immediately and the bounded background write degraded alone — DB degradation converts 1:1 into anonymous-access outage.

[ADVISORY] The updateDevice success path — an existing in-window device re-tagging while at the limit, the behavior every returning visitor depends on — is never exercised; TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers the 0-rows-affected denial for a nonexistent device. A regression in updateDevice's WHERE window or SET clause (e.g., an inverted bound) locks every existing anonymous device out once the limit is reached while the suite stays green.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour is declared identically in two packages — anonstore/database.go:16 (count/expire window) and anonimpl/api/api.go:17 (ListDevices listing window) — same name, coupled-but-distinct windows, no single source of truth. An editor changing the store's retention silently desyncs the API listing window (or vice versa) with no compile error, and the shared name hides that the two windows are governed independently.

[ADVISORY] The Go DTO always serializes anonymousDeviceLimit as a number (0 when disabled) while the TS side declares `number | undefined` with a boot default of undefined, giving the same state two wire representations with no consumer in this diff to pin the semantics. The first frontend consumer must guess whether 0 and undefined both mean 'unlimited'; an `=== undefined` check treats a current backend (always sends 0) differently from a payload missing the field, silently inverting the feature for that consumer.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now constructs AnonDBStore internally from cfg instead of receiving the injectable anonstore.AnonStore parameter, removing the provider-injection seam the codebase's DI pattern provides. AnonDeviceService can no longer be exercised with a fake store (every test now requires InitTestDB) and is hard-wired to the DB implementation even though the AnonStore interface still exists for the API half; a wire provider for the store reading cfg would have preserved the seam.

[ADVISORY] The goroutine's recover() guard was removed along with the goroutine, so a panic inside TagDevice now propagates into the authn middleware instead of being logged and swallowed. Any panic in the tagging path turns every anonymous request into a 500 for as long as it persists, where the previous code logged a warning and served the request.

[ADVISORY] The limit check runs CountDevices before knowing whether the device exists, so every returning device pays COUNT + UPDATE/UPSERT where an update-first ordering (UPDATE; on 0 rows COUNT, then INSERT or deny) serves the dominant case with one statement and identical semantics. At the limit, every cache-expired returning device executes two statements instead of one on the auth path; across a large anonymous fleet this redundant COUNT is the main added database load of the feature.

[BUG] Review iterations silently inverted the tagging execution model: anonymous device tagging was fire-and-forget (detached goroutine on context.Background(), 2-minute timeoutTag cap, panic recovery, errors only logged) and is now synchronous DB I/O executed inside Authenticate on every anonymous request — including when device_limit is left at the default 0, i.e. when the feature this PR adds is switched off — enabled by flipping TagDevice's contract from swallow-all to propagate-all in impl.go. Every cache-miss anonymous request now blocks on the device upsert (plus a COUNT when a limit is configured) before authentication returns, so a slow or hung database stalls anonymous page loads instead of degrading silently in the background as before; the 2-minute cap and panic recovery are also gone, so a panic in the tagging path now kills the response. Operators who accepted 'add a configurable device limit' did not accept 'device writes move into the request path for all anonymous traffic even with the limit disabled'.

[BUG] The objective silently expanded from 'limit tracked devices' to 'deny anonymous access': when the store reports the limit reached, Authenticate returns an error instead of the anonymous identity, so the request fails authentication — inverting the anonymous client's previous unconditional identity-on-enabled behavior, with no user-facing mapping of the raw 'device limit reached' error and no test above the store layer pinning the decision. An operator who sets device_limit to cap device tracking turns their public anonymous instance into one that rejects new visitors once the cap is hit (traffic spike, shared NAT/proxy rotation): those requests proceed with no identity and are rejected by authorization, and every denied request additionally logs an authentication-failure error. The only new test exercises the store directly, so the access-denial decision — the actual teeth of the feature — shipped with nothing pinning what a visitor experiences.

[BUG] updateDevice's BETWEEN window is anchored on the caller-supplied device.UpdatedAt with only a +1 minute forward allowance, so a known device whose stored updated_at is more than 1 minute ahead of the evaluating instance's clock (cross-instance clock skew, or any caller passing a stale UpdatedAt as the new test itself does with -1h) matches 0 rows and is reported as ErrDeviceLimitReached. In multi-instance deployments without sticky sessions the per-instance local cache does not mask cross-instance hits, so a returning device that is under the limit gets intermittently denied anonymous access whenever the instance evaluating the update has a clock more than ~1 minute behind the one that last wrote the row — a flaky lockout that looks like the limit being hit when it isn't.

[BUG] The limit is enforced with an unsynchronized count-then-insert: CountDevices and the INSERT run in separate sessions with no transaction or lock, so concurrent first-touch devices all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert. Under a burst of new devices (crawler, traffic spike, several instances serving simultaneously) the enforced device count overshoots the configured device_limit by the size of the race window, so the accepted constraint 'at most N devices' is only approximately enforced and operators relying on a hard cap get more than N rows.

[ADVISORY] The review-driven rename of thirtyDays to anonymousDeviceExpiration in api.go leaves two independent definitions of the same 30-day constant — this one (ListDevices display window) and anonstore/database.go:16 (limit-enforcement window) — instead of a single source of truth. When the expiration next changes (e.g., made configurable), whoever updates the enforcement constant has no signal that the API window has its own copy, and the device list shown to admins silently disagrees with the window the limit actually enforces over.

[ADVISORY] The frontend plumbing for anonymousDeviceLimit ships inert and type-mismatched: the Go DTO serializes an int64 unconditionally (0 when unset, no omitempty) so the value is never undefined on the wire, nothing in the diff consumes it client-side, and the configured capacity is exposed to every visitor via boot data. Future readers take 'number | undefined' and the '= undefined' class default as the contract and write undefined-checks that can never trigger; meanwhile any visitor can read the instance's anonymous device capacity from window.grafanaBootData with no feature to show for it.

[ADVISORY] The only new test covers the store-level 'second new device denied' path; the feature's core happy path — a known device returning while at the limit must match the BETWEEN window, be updated, and keep access — plus the client-level error routing and the localcache-vs-limit interaction are untouched (the test deliberately bypasses the service layer where the cache lives). A regression in updateDevice's window bounds, or in the cache population order relative to the store call (e.g., a denied device being cached and then granted access on retry, defeating the limit), would ship green: no test in the diff fails, and the first signal would be operators reporting flaky lockouts or a limit that does not hold.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (independent 2-minute timeout, panic recovery) into the synchronous Authenticate path, so every anonymous cache-miss request now performs its COUNT/INSERT/UPDATE database round trips inline before authentication completes. A slow or hung database now stalls anonymous requests on the unauthenticated hot path that previously completed independently of tagging (the removed goroutine used context.Background() precisely so tagging could not block auth), and a panic inside the tagging code that was previously recovered and logged now propagates into the request and surfaces as a 500 — an availability regression for every deployment with anonymous access, including the default deviceLimit=0 configuration where the limit buys nothing.

[ADVISORY] The device limit is enforced against a client-controlled identifier — device_id originates from the anonymous device cookie the client sends, so the limit provides no abuse boundary: an unauthenticated attacker creates devices at will by rotating cookie values and can deliberately register device_limit forged devices. Once forged devices fill the limit, every new anonymous device hits ErrDeviceLimitReached and anonymous authentication is denied — a trivially cheap lockout DoS against anonymous access that persists until rows age out of the ~61-day cleanup horizon or an operator raises the limit, while the attacker himself defeats the limit entirely by rotating IDs, so the feature costs availability without constraining abuse.

[ADVISORY] Limit enforcement is check-then-act: CountDevices and the subsequent INSERT run as separate unsynchronized statements with no transaction or lock, so concurrent cache-miss requests all observe count < limit and all insert. A burst of concurrent requests (e.g., an attacker spraying forged device IDs in parallel, since each request is unauthenticated and unthrottled) overshoots the configured limit by an unbounded amount in a single burst, so the device count this feature exists to cap is not actually bounded.

[BUG] updateDevice treats RowsAffected()==0 as 'device not found', but on MySQL RowsAffected reports changed rows rather than matched rows, so an UPDATE that matches an existing in-window device but changes no values (same-second re-tag with identical client_ip/user_agent/updated_at, e.g. parallel requests after local-cache expiry in an HA setup) returns 0 and is misreported as ErrDeviceLimitReached. When the device limit is reached on MySQL, requests from an already-known device within the 30-day window are spuriously denied anonymous authentication whenever a concurrent duplicate UPDATE lands in the same timestamp tick — flaky auth failures for legitimate anonymous users that the Postgres/SQLite paths do not exhibit.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day retention constant is now duplicated: anonymousDeviceExpiration is defined in anonstore/database.go (line 16) and again in anonimpl/api/api.go (line 17, replacing thirtyDays), with no shared definition linking the limit-count window to the admin list window. A future change to the retention window edited in only one package silently desynchronizes the limit-count/update window from the ListDevices API window, producing devices that count against the limit but are inconsistently represented in the admin device listing — the next change gets riskier because two hand-maintained copies must be edited in lockstep.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only exercises the reject-new-device path: it creates two distinct device IDs and never re-tags an existing device while the limit is reached, so updateDevice's success branch (rowsAffected > 0, database.go:95-97) — the behavior that keeps existing anonymous users working once the limit is hit — is never executed by any test in the diff (checked: database_test.go and impl_test.go are the only test files; no other test reaches updateDevice). If the UPDATE's WHERE window or SET clause regresses so it matches zero rows for existing devices, every anonymous device — including returning ones — gets ErrDeviceLimitReached and is locked out of anonymous access entirely, while the suite stays green; the test also never asserts storage state after rejection (that device 'keep' was not inserted).

[ADVISORY] The new rejection branch in Anonymous.Authenticate (`if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) { return nil, err }`) is exercised by no test: the only test-shaped files in the diff (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go) never construct the Anonymous client or call Authenticate, and impl_test.go's TagDevice tests build the service with setting.NewCfg() whose AnonymousDeviceLimit is 0, so the limit error can never reach this branch (a pre-existing test also cannot cover it — the error type is new in this diff). This is the diff's most user-visible behavior change — anonymous requests beyond the limit now fail authentication — and it has zero coverage; a regression that demotes the limit error to the warn-and-continue path (the exact behavior this diff removes) silently re-admits anonymous users beyond the limit while the suite stays green.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice's contract changed from infallible to fallible — the new `return err` at line 147 is the only path carrying ErrDeviceLimitReached from the store up to Authenticate — yet impl_test.go still asserts require.NoError on every TagDevice call and runs with AnonymousDeviceLimit 0, so no test exercises TagDevice returning an error. If `return err` regresses to the old swallow-and-return-nil behavior, ErrDeviceLimitReached never reaches Authenticate and the device limit silently stops rejecting anyone, while every service-level test (which asserts NoError universally) still passes.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device window is now defined twice as two independent constants with the same name and value — anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go:16 and in anonimpl/api/api.go:17 (renamed from thirtyDays) — with no shared source of truth. If one constant changes without the other, devices counted against the device limit fall outside the admin list API's window (or vice versa), so operators see fewer devices than are actually consuming the limit and cannot identify or delete the offenders via the API.

[ADVISORY] The goroutine wrapper around TagDevice was removed together with its recover() and 2-minute timeout, so tagging now runs synchronously inside Authenticate: a panic in tagging — previously recovered and logged — now propagates into the authentication path, and the per-device DB upsert (plus the COUNT query when device_limit > 0) now blocks authentication on local-cache misses instead of running in the background. Anonymous requests on cache miss (every ~15-29 minutes per device) now wait on DB roundtrips before authentication completes, and a tagging panic that was previously a logged warning becomes a failed request (500 via the HTTP recover middleware); no test in the diff pins the new synchronous/error-propagating execution model.

[ADVISORY] The TS contract promises `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` with an `undefined` default (and the interface at grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 types it optional), but the only producer — FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 with no omitempty — always serializes a number (0 when unset), so the undefined state is unreachable from a real Grafana backend; the field also has no reader anywhere in this diff. Frontend code branching on `undefined` (e.g., 'limit not configured') is dead in production, and any frontend test that omits the field verifies a state the backend can never send — the Go DTO and TS type are a hand-maintained pair already drifted at birth.

[ADVISORY] No test verifies that devices aging out of the 30-day window free limit slots: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit uses only fresh (-1h) devices, so the count window's lower bound at database.go:110 — the mechanism that prevents the limit from becoming a permanent ratchet — is never exercised (CountDevices takes from/to as parameters, so any pre-existing test of it does not pin the window the limit flow passes). A regression that counts stale devices (or never frees slots) permanently locks out all new anonymous devices once N devices have ever been seen, with the suite green; a test that backdates a device's updated_at beyond 30 days and asserts a new device can then be created would pin this semantic.

[BUG] Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no deadline, so anon-store DB latency, lock contention (e.g., the periodic DeleteDevicesOlderThan cleanup deleting from anon_device), or connection-pool exhaustion stalls every cache-miss anonymous authentication, where previously the tag ran in a background goroutine with context.Background(), a 2-minute timeoutTag cap, and never delayed the response. Anonymous page loads and API requests block for as long as the anon_device write takes — the 2-minute cap was removed entirely, so a hung or slow anon_device table hangs anonymous authentication indefinitely; and because the sync call is not gated on the limit, this latency coupling is imposed even on deployments with device_limit=0 where the feature is disabled and the sync error buys nothing (non-limit errors are still just logged).

[ADVISORY] The recover() that contained panics in the tagging path was deleted along with the goroutine, so a panic inside TagDevice now propagates out of Authenticate into the authn flow instead of being contained as the 'Tag anon session panic' warning. A panic bug in the anon store or tagging code aborts every cache-miss anonymous request (net/http kills the connection with no response) instead of logging a warning and serving the request — failure containment on the anonymous auth hot path is lost for all deployments, not just those with the limit enabled.

[ADVISORY] With device_limit enabled, every cache-miss request runs a COUNT aggregate over anon_device before the upsert, and devices rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached are never cached (TagDevice returns at the new early `return err` in impl.go before the success tail that sets localCache), so each request from a beyond-limit device repeats CountDevices plus a 0-row UPDATE. DB load concentrates exactly on the rejected clients with no negative caching or backoff: once a deployment hits its limit, every retry from every blocked device costs two anon_device queries including a range COUNT over the table, for as long as those clients keep polling.

[ADVISORY] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-insert check (no transaction or lock between the count at line 90 and the insert below), so concurrent first-time devices at the boundary all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert. An operator who sets device_limit=N gets a soft cap: a burst of simultaneous new devices (flash crowd, crawler with fresh cookies) silently overshoots N by the width of the race window and the extra rows persist until cleanup, contradicting the hard cap the config option promises.

[ADVISORY] When the device limit rejects a device, the only log on the path is TagDevice's Debug-level 'Failed to tag device for UI' and the new client.go branch (lines 45-47) returns the error to the authn flow without logging anything, so at default (info) verbosity limit rejections leave no trace. An operator who sets device_limit too low (or forgets it is set) sees anonymous users silently bounced to login with zero log evidence at info level, making the misconfiguration and any unexplained drop in anonymous traffic hard to diagnose.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device window is now declared twice — anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go line 16 and an identically-named constant in anonimpl/api/api.go line 17 — with nothing tying the limit's counting/refresh window to the admin ListDevices window. A future change to one constant silently desyncs the two windows: devices counted by the limit but invisible in the ListDevices admin API (or vice versa), misdirecting debugging of 'why is the limit full when the API lists fewer devices'.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff exercises updateDevice's success path — an existing device with updated_at inside the 30-day window being refreshed while count >= deviceLimit (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers the 0-rows rejection, and every other test constructs the store with deviceLimit 0, skipping the limit branch entirely). A regression in the UPDATE's window bounds or SET columns would reject every existing anonymous device the moment the limit is reached — mass lockout of returning users on every cache expiry (~29 minutes) — and no test in the diff would catch it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no deadline, so anon-store DB latency, lock contention (e.g., the periodic DeleteDevicesOlderThan cleanup deleting from anon_device), or connection-pool exhaustion stalls every cache-miss anonymous authentication, where previously the tag ran in a background goroutine with context.Background(), a 2-minute timeoutTag cap, and never delayed the response.
